description.value: Airport Inn is a renovated motel situated just minutes from the Port Hardy Airport and the BC Ferries terminal — a critical gateway for cyclists completing a Vancouver Island tour or connecting to Prince Rupert. The property offers a range of room types including kitchenette units suited for extended stays, along with an on-site restaurant, liquor store, and meeting rooms. Its location near the northern terminus of Island cycling routes makes it a strategically important stop in an area with limited accommodation options.

address.value: 4030 Byng Road, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is fully accessible and corroborates all OSM contact details (address, phone, website). The site describes amenities including free high-speed Wi-Fi (also confirmed by OSM internet_access=wlan), an on-site restaurant, complimentary continental breakfast, and free airport shuttle, but contains no mention of bike storage, bike procedures, laundry, drying areas, e-bike charging, or any other cycling-specific facilities. Required criteria for WWC accreditation (secure bike storage, staff bike procedure) cannot be confirmed from any evidence source.
concerns: OSM name is 'Airport Inn' but the website consistently uses 'Airport Inn - Port Hardy' or 'Airport Inn-Port Hardy' as the full business name.
No cycling-specific amenities (bike storage, bike handling, tools, wash) are mentioned anywhere on the website; both required criteria are unverifiable without direct contact.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate motel at a key cycling gateway (northern Vancouver Island ferry terminal) that would be valuable to touring cyclists, but neither required WWC criterion — secure bike storage and staff bike procedure knowledge — can be confirmed from the website. Direct outreach is needed to determine if the property can meet WWC requirements.
enrichment_extras.notes: Property is a strategic overnight stop for cyclists at the northern end of Vancouver Island, near the BC Ferries terminal to Prince Rupert. A direct inquiry about bike storage arrangements would likely resolve the required criteria quickly.
